main_text.p: ducunque, siue aperte, siue oblique quicquid labefa- ctant[?] ex doctrina tradita. Hæc Bellarminus.

Num quis existimare potest, hunc hominem ex animo loqui, aut serio de his rebus cogitasse, qui non erubuit Patrum verba ad sententiam suam confirmandam producere, quæ causam ipsam jugulant, quam illi confirmare voluit. Anathema dicit Apostolus euangelizanti præter id, quod accepimus. Bellarminus ait, præter hic intelligi contra. At Patres ab eo producti clamant magno consensu: Apostolum non dicere, qui contraria annuntiauerint, sed qui aliquid vel oblique labefactant, hoc anathemate perstringi. Num quid apertius? Præter ergo, ex eorum consensu, non est tantum contra Euangelium, sed & præter Euangelium; quia, judice Bellarmino, hoc anathemate feriuntur, non tantum qui contra Euangelium, sed etiam, qui paulo aliter docent.
Eâdem[?] fronte Basilium & Augustinum adducit. S. Basilius Moral. 72. cap. 1[?] docet, ex hoc loco haberi, eos recipiendos, qui consona Scripturis tradunt, eos reiiciendos, qui aliena.

Respondeo: S. Basilius probat, Pontificios el-se homines profanos, qui ea de fide tradere audeant, quæ Scripturis non sunt consona, sed aliena. Mirificus videtur thaumaturgus, qui ex his verbis probabit, nova dogmata esse recipienda, quæ aliena sunt, non autem consona Scripturis. page.notes: Page heavily stained and blurred on the right and centre; several words are doubtful and marked [?]. The page number "31" is partly obscured. The running head "CAPVT IV." is clear. The first line of the page has partly lost letters at the start ("ducunque"), and the last word of the first paragraph is uncertain ("labefactant"). "cap. 1" in the Basilius reference may be "I". "el-se" at the line break after "Pontificios" is uncertain. The left sliver of the neighbouring page was excluded as instructed.
